headline: PHP 8.6 Tightens Types and Opens I/O
lede: PHP 8.6 brings partial application, nanosecond durations, native polling, and stricter APIs. Migration work follows: several legacy behaviors and interfaces are leaving the runtime behind.

headline: Ruby’s ß Bug Opens Rails to RCE
lede: A one-byte heap overflow in legacy encoding handling turns attacker-controlled text into a pre-authentication remote-code-execution path. Upgrade Ruby immediately; unsupported 3.2 and older releases remain exposed.

headline: Europe Runs Matrix Across 40,000 Desks
lede: The European Commission has put a self-operated Matrix service in the hands of more than 40,000 staff. Sovereignty here means more than hosting: it includes operational control, resilience, procurement leverage, and the hard work of making federation scale.

headline: SQLite Shards Turn Blobs Into a System
lede: Blobasaur replaces a brittle single-node store with sharded SQLite, Rust, compression, and careful batching. The result is roughly 2 ms p99 latency on three nodes—an economical answer to a very specific workload.

headline: Gemini 4 Neon Targets Long-Running Work
lede: Google’s Gemini 4 Neon arrives with a million-token context window, adjustable reasoning, and a $3-per-million-input-token price. It is positioned for software engineering, scientific analysis, and agents that must keep working after the first prompt.

headline: Storage Prices Wait on the AI Cycle
lede: NAND supply may loosen in late 2027, while hard-drive relief could take another year. The forecast is less a promise than a reminder that factories, contracts, and AI demand move on different clocks.
pullquote: The cheapest upgrade may be the one you postpone.

headline: A Garage Door Escapes the Cloud
lede: A ratgdo32 board returns a myQ garage opener to local control, with HomeKit, Tailscale, and overnight Slack checks layered on top. The build replaces ads and vendor dependence with a small, inspectable automation system.

headline: NGINX HTTP/2 Bugs Put Gateways at Risk
lede: Two unauthenticated memory-corruption flaws can turn an ordinary NGINX gateway into an entry point for code execution. Patch fixed releases now, or disable HTTP/2 while internet-facing systems move to the front of the queue.

headline: One VM Hosts 15 Million Web Servers
lede: A single CPU core and 10 GB of RAM are not enough for conventional processes, but they can support a radically leaner runtime. With smoltcp and user-space networking, the experiment passes sixteen million minimal servers by discarding assumptions the kernel normally carries for you.

headline: Compress Memory Before Buying More RAM
lede: zram turns compressed memory into extra working room, trading some CPU time and latency for a longer life on fixed hardware. One test fit 5.7 GB of data into 1.7 GB of RAM—a useful margin when browser tabs are winning.
